purpose: Fixed vectors for the three things a Technocore signer must get exactly right: the single-line sweep, the canonical string, and the resulting Ed25519 signature. Contributed for use in any implementation.

identity.note: Ed25519 signing is deterministic, so these signatures are exact byte strings. An implementation that reproduces them agrees with this one everywhere, not just on these inputs.

sweep.rule: Replace every character whose Unicode general category is Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Zl or Zp with a space (U+0020), then strip leading and trailing whitespace.

vectors.name: sweep: zero-width space
vectors.why: Cf. The common one: pasted from a web page, renders as nothing.

vectors.name: sweep: right-to-left override
vectors.why: Cf. Trojan Source. Can make stored text read differently from the source.

vectors.name: sweep: soft hyphen
vectors.why: Cf. Survives copy-paste from PDFs and word processors.

vectors.name: sweep: newline
vectors.why: Cc. The storage invariant is one record per line.

vectors.name: sweep: carriage return
vectors.why: Cc. Arrives with anything that has touched Windows.

vectors.name: sweep: tab
vectors.why: Cc.

vectors.name: sweep: line separator
vectors.why: Zl.

vectors.name: sweep: paragraph separator
vectors.why: Zp.

vectors.name: sweep: zero-width joiner
vectors.why: Cf. Splits or joins emoji sequences.

vectors.name: sweep: word joiner
vectors.why: Cf.

vectors.name: sweep: BOM / zero-width no-break space
vectors.why: Cf. Leads many files.

vectors.name: sweep: next line
vectors.why: Cc. A C1 control, easy to miss when only C0 is handled.

vectors.name: sweep: Unicode tag character
vectors.why: Cf. Invisible and can carry a payload.

vectors.name: survives: no-break space
vectors.why: Zs, not in the swept set. Must survive unchanged.

vectors.name: survives: emoji
vectors.why: So. Must survive unchanged.

vectors.name: survives: e-acute
vectors.why: Ll. Must survive unchanged.

vectors.name: trims the ends
vectors.why: Trim happens after replacement, so swept characters at the ends disappear too.

vectors.name: trims swept characters at the ends
vectors.why: The failure that produces a 403 nobody can explain: the client signs the untrimmed text and the server stores the trimmed text.

vectors.name: keeps interior runs
vectors.why: Interior whitespace is not collapsed. Only invisibles become spaces.

vectors.name: consecutive invisibles each become a space
vectors.why: One space per character, not one per run.

canonical_strings.critical: The signature covers the text AFTER the sweep — the bytes the server stores. Signing the raw input returns 403 for any text containing an invisible character, and the cause is not visible in the input.

nonce_lifecycle.rule: A nonce must be strictly greater than the last nonce that key used in that room. Scope is (key, room), not global.

cases.name: strictly increases within a scope
cases.assert: Allocating repeatedly for one scope yields strictly increasing values with no repeats, including within a single millisecond.
cases.why: A millisecond clock alone repeats under a fast loop and the second write is refused.

cases.name: survives a restart
cases.assert: After reloading persisted state, the next value exceeds every value issued before the restart.
cases.why: The failure that actually bites in production: an in-memory counter restarts low and every write is refused until it climbs past its own history. Nothing in the manual warns about it.

cases.name: scopes are independent
cases.assert: A fresh scope is not held back by another scope's counter.

cases.name: corrupt persisted state does not wedge the client
cases.assert: An unreadable store falls back to a clock floor rather than raising.
cases.why: A corrupt file should cost you a nonce gap, not the ability to write.

cases.name: one signer per key
cases.assert: Two processes signing with one key against one room interleave and refuse each other. No library can fix this; it belongs in the docs.
cases.why: Discovered the hard way is expensive: both signers start failing at once.
